reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds, so I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 260, 263, 265 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the order list to identify the customers to pay.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly. The orders name three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first, since the task says to use net_balance rather than doing the arithmetic myself.

Acme's net balance is 21828. Let me verify with the numbers: orders 25692 + 20673 = 46365, minus refunds 8294 + 16243 = 24537, giving 21828. That matches, so the figure is consistent. I'll record the payout for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch and cobalt remain, so I'll get birch's net balance next.
Birch's net balance is 62075. Birch has no refunds, and orders 32750 + 29325 = 62075, so the figure checks out. I'll record the payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The only customer left is cobalt, so I'll get cobalt's net balance from net_balance before recording its payout.

Cobalt's net balance is 39438. Its orders total 33488 + 16853 = 50341, less the 10903 refund on order 265, which gives 39438, so the figure checks out. I'll record cobalt's payout, the last one in the batch.
All three customers have been paid: acme, birch, and cobalt. Each net balance matched my own check against the orders and refunds, so I'm finishing with the payout map.
